## once the $TERM is unset, it works fine

Hmm. That's sortof expected. If `$TERM` is not set, I believe nvim will fall back on some basic tty name like "dumb" or "vt100". This reïnforces my suspicion that the problem is related to some values obtained from your terminfo.

Good day,

Can it be fixed on the part of the neovim by any chance?

It still happening. But I can open Nvim inside Tmux.

Tmux as default will change $TERM to `screen `, is this a clue?

It depends on `$TERM`, as explained above. (edit: more precisely, it depends on the values in your terminfo database, which depend on `$TERM`)

It is working again with St. 

I wiped my SSD and reinstalled Arch Linux and St again.

might be a windows virus! . Got rid of it  for good! haha

I had this issue as well, but based on the comment from @oldgaro I took a look at the commits on st since I originally compiled. I ended up cherry-picking https://git.suckless.org/st/commit/?id=b331da550b290d54592b7ba11242c92f5a303a48 into my st source. I then ran "tic -sx st.info" to get updated terminfo information and this fixed the issue.

This appears to be a libtermkey issue triggered by st's terminfo configuration prior to commit b331da5 in st.

Cheers,

I also just encountered this bug while trying to update my st installation to current master with some patches.
neovim: v0.2.0 (gentoo-ebuild)
st commit: b1338e91ed632adbcd08388de37e46cf25326e01

The patch I believe to cause issues on my end is the following: https://st.suckless.org/patches/delkey/
The version I applied is this one: https://st.suckless.org/patches/delkey/st-delkey-20160727-308bfbf.diff

Running with the patch I cannot get nvim to start (same error as described above) and have some trouble regarding terminal input for sudo and other interactive dialogues. Without the patch everything works as usual and no issues occur. So anyone using the patch, I advise you to revert it and not use it anymore (I cannot find a reason as to why it should be required. On my end everything as expected).

I have little understanding as to why this happens but I believe this to be a multi-component issue in the end.

@mvaenskae Might be it indeed, cause I did patch St with delkey too! haha

PS: I found that most St patches are pretty much not that important, so now I am using St vanilla with Atom one colorscheme and Profont...
